tips.comment: Samra Star is the rank outsider of the field and requires something of a leap of faith, but I can't let her go unbacked at 80/1. She has been pulling her hard when racing for the stable which has been under a cloud for much of the season but there are signs that things are starting to turn around now and she has a piece of form in the book for her previous trainer which gives her every chance here. The drop back in trip is also a positive and she's often been at the front or close to it before fading when racing over further. The win on the AW in a novice race was less than a year ago and quite simply, anything within about 10lb of that run would be good enough to win this. She easily beat a horse that's since won off 92 and several others are now 80+ rated horses so Samra Star's mark of 68 is actually a very winnable one if she settles and returns to something like that level again.

Backing The Caltonian, the 6??'year??'old Swiss Spirit gelding trained by Linda Perratt, in tomorrow’s Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Handicap (Class 4, 6f) at Ayr. He makes his seasonal bow after a 79??'day break, following a competitive winter campaign on all??'weather where he won back-to-back 6f handicaps at Newcastle in January??'clearly showing he can deliver well when fresh and at this trip. His April 18 return outing (11th of 14 in a Newcastle grade??'2 sprint) wasn’t ideal, but he'd been held up and brushed through congested running, so I'd expect him to be sharper this time.
He’s well experienced at Ayr too??'with five career runs here, including a 3rd, 4th, and 2nd in 2023??'24??'suggesting he handles the track and draw. Set to be ridden by Kaiya Fraser.

Doesn't always work out when you have a long traveler, but they do catch the eye. That is exactly the case with Unico, who travels all the way from Hampshire. Has form on good to soft, and with 5 places on offer, surely he must place to pay for that huge journey.

This horse is ground dependent since she clearly runs her better races on softish ground, which is something she's not had since switching stables. As a result she's now slipped 5lb since the switch in yards and is now 5lb lower than her last good run which was a 3rd of 15 on soft when beaten less than 2 lengths. The new trainer has also booked a very useful Apprentice now who is able to take another 7lb off so under her ideal conditions here she could outrun her 20/1 odds.
Over at NightmAyr, the form of Billy No Mates looks solid enough and gets a nice claimer up to boost the tip. The track throws some tardy stuff up, though, but it has won on course.
Unbeaten in 3 starts for Olly Murphy over fences in handicaps and has winning form for previous stable here. Surely will be hard to beat if taking to the smaller obstacles in a weak novice.

The model I run suggests Mighty Fleur can win this one. Mighty Fleur lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other runners but steps out carrying a rock bottom weight. This leaves Mighty Fleur working off an attractive mark. Very consistent placing history of 2323 but needs to find a bit more to get over the line first. Hasn't run in 88 days and needs to go well fresh. Shane Fenelon on board claims a further 5 lbs and this makes sure Mighty Fleur carries the lowest weight in the field by 5 lbs around this 2m 4f trip. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Placed 11th in a bumper at Bangor on his NH debut about 16 days ago. He is now set to make his hurdles debut, but he has significant improvement to make. Adam Wedge will be riding him this time, which I think will suit the 5-year-old better. Jack Tudor appeared to take him in too early while pursuing the leaders and he was outpaced 2f out. This gelding will have benefited from that outing, and at 125/1 for an each-way bet, he warrants another chance.

The model I run suggests Nickelforce can win this one. Nickelforce lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 9 runner field but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated off this mark. Is not penalised in the weights for the higher RPR and official rankings and has shown some form coming into this. Charlie Case picks up the reins and claims a further 7 lbs which is helpful around this longer 2m 7f trip. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

This Jamie Snowden-trained 6-year-old gelding has won three hurdle races from two miles to two miles four furlongs on good to firm and good ground. The latest was over this course and distance on good ground 19 days ago when leading from the start and keeping on well in the closing stages to beat the O Murphy-trained Ukantango by five lengths. With G Sheehan back onboard, he can follow up today.

The model I run suggests Ukantango can win this one. Ukantango lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other runners but has an official ranking that is second last. This subsequently means Ukantango goes out carrying the second lowest amount of weight around this 2m 4f trip. Running for the second time post wind op and came a decent second place after the first run out 19 days ago. Needs to come on from that but possible with the champion jockey Sean Bowen on board. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

This Jamie Snowden-trained 8-year-old mare has improved in her three hurdle races, coming back from a 334-day break over two miles four furlongs on good to firm and good to soft ground. The latest was over this course and distance 25 days ago when leading from the start to easily beat the James Owen-trained Back In The Bay by eight lengths. With G Sheehan in the saddle, she could prove a hard nut to crack.

The model I run suggests Boskill Borden can win this one. Boskill Borden lines up here with the second highest RPR of the field but an official ranking that is third lowest. This leaves Boskill Borden carrying significantly less weight than the other runners near the top of the order around this 2m 4f round trip. Has shown some reasonable form in the latest run with a good second place finish 12 days ago. Wheeled out again in quick succession to try and push on, and Shane Fenelon picks up the reins, relieving a further 5lb for claiming. This takes the total weight differential to the market favourite to be 1 stone 7 lbs, which can be telling over the distance. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Redbridge Rambler should win this one. Redbridge Rambler lines up here with the highest RPR and the highest official ranking, but isn't penalized for it in the weights. The weight differential to all runners here apart from 2 horses is only 5 lbs around this 2m 4f trip. Champion Jockey Sean Bowen picks up the reins and is a trusted pair of hands. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, and this translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Sporty Jim can win this one. Sporty Jim lines up here with the highest RPR of the 10 runners but is middle order in official ranking. This leaves Sporty Jim working off an attractive mark and carries 1 stone less than the top weight and current market leader Fine By Me. Sporty Jim ran a decent third 30 days ago but needs to come on from that to get over the line first. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Going by stablemate G’Day Aussie completing a double at Bangor the other day at the age of 12, it looks like the stable are flying again.
STAMINA CHOPE has filled the runner-up spot on her last two visits to this course and I’m hopeful of a big run operating off a career-low mark. Crazy price in what looks a weak affair.
In the form of her life having won three of her last four races. The 6 lbs increase might not be enough to stop her achieving the hat-trick here.

This was quite the gamble in a hot race for the grade over 2m4f at Uttoxeter last month. Although she could only finish third after being too keen early on, the first/second have franked the form since. Champion jockey Sean Bowen is now in the saddle and it will be interesting to see how they ride her down in trip. I'm pretty surprised by the price, one I thought would be close to favourite.

Auntie Maggie made all unchallenged at Uttoxeter last time. But Bluebella, who ran on to snatch second on the line, could reverse that form on six pounds better terms. Her jumping was better than usual at Uttoxeter, and a similar display at Worcester should see her go close off the same low mark of 76.

This has to be one of my strongest fancies for some time. Finished 4th last time out after a 6-month break. The first, second, and third have all come out of that race and won, so the form is excellent. The icing on the cake is she goes back into mares' company here.

I mentioned in another race how this stable seem to be on the upturn, so I really have to give this one a shot given it won last year's renewal off 2lb higher. Hopefully it's been laid out and will bounce back to form on the back of a wind procedure.
A lot in here that will cut each other's throats, so one that will avoid trouble, it seems, is the David O'Meara runner Sea Regal, which looks ready to go close again.

Gelded son of Hunter's Light & Cherina Dynamite ( Dam's sire Kodiac ) who was last seen at Wetherby 18 days ago where finishing a respectable 6th/11 and did shape better than that bare result suggests and watching that race very carefully Jez Bomb most certainly needed a stronger gallop on the occasion and a good analysis of this class 5 handicap clearly shows Jez Bomb is likely to get that stronger gallop here given the horses enrolled to run here and that can play well into his strengths here at the Ripon track currently operating on a mark of 64 which is well within range S England's inmate is more than capable of getting back on the score boards and possess all the necessary credentials to take a race of this nature jockey C Horgan takes off a very valuable looking 5lb which only enhances his good looking claims here price at the time of writing represents good E/W value bold showing is anticipated

Backing Mr Jetman, the 5-year-old Territories gelding trained by Seb Spencer, in the 1-mile Class 5 handicap at Ripon. He’s proven at this course, having won here twice this season??'a cosy victory on 4 June and another smart win in a Class 6 on 18 May??'both over this same trip on good ground .
Since stepping up in grade on 19 June, he still ran well, finishing 5th of 8 over 1m 1f??'only just beaten . Now off a mark of 61, he returns to his favoured mile at Ripon, where his record stands at 2 wins from 2 runs, and connections have booked Jack Dace, whose 5-lb claim could prove decisive in a close contest.
Expect him to settle handy, benefit from a strong gallop, and produce his well-known sustained finish up the straight.
Billy Loughnane takes over on the class dropper Zarzyni here. Although it doesn't look like a next-time winner, it should do a lot better today.

Gelded son of Soldier's call & La Vale ( Dam's sire Freedom Child ) who began his career impressively with his first three career starts reading 212 resulting in him beginning life in handicaps on a mark of 81 at the time a mark of 81 was a bit too heavy for this sort of individual however he was last seen at Redcar 16 days ago where racing on a reduced mark of 73 and he really threatened to get competitive where finishing 4th/8 and most certainly shaped better than that bare result suggests and the manor he kept on with between horses was actually quite impressive in my books and he looks ready to take advantage of his rapidly easing mark as the handicapper has eased him a further 2lb and he is now operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 71 M & D Easterby's inmate looks poised to strike of this sort of mark jockey Lewis Chalkley takes off a very valuable looking 7lb which only enhances his good looking claims here merits consideration
Has won previously over course and distance and looks likely to appreciate this step back up in distance. Runs off a reasonable looking mark.
Won debut hurdle run in style, in a very quick-timed event, beating today's rivals by a clear 5 seconds. Connections rate this horse very much, including a statement it is a 'Summer Horse'.

The Cian Collins 6-year-old hurdler narrowly failed to land a touch at Kilbeggan 36 days ago following a break of five months. Following a maiden hurdle win at Sligo last July on his debut over the obstacles, he was allotted a mark of 116, which seemed and proved to be excessive. Since then, he's dropped 16 lb in the weights, and he's remained on 100 following that third at the beginning of June. I think connections will be eager to regain their losses from then.

Moon Mariner is a 5-year-old daughter of Sea Moon ex Sarah's Cottage, thus a half-sister to Super Duty by Shantou. She makes her racecourse debut here in this Lady Riders Mares Bumper. She'll be ridden by Miss J Townend for WP Mullins. She may be one for your horse tracker. The stable is in top form at the moment. I make her my nap of the day.
Barra Rua ran a nice first race finishing 2nd in a good looking bumper at Limerick just over a month ago for Emmet Mullins. He is nicely related and with some improvement can go well here.
